title: Water on Earth and the Water Cycle
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Water on Earth and the Water Cycle Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
short_title: Water on Earth and the water cycle
standard_text: Describe the distribution of water on Earth; explain the water cycle and the factors that drive it; describe watersheds, groundwater and how water systems affect climate. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Water Systems)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on fresh and salt water, the water cycle, watersheds, groundwater, the Great Lakes and water and climate. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Only about 3% of Earth's water is fresh.
key_sub: The Sun and gravity drive the water cycle; every place on land is in a watershed.
body_html:
How to think about it

About 97% of Earth's water is salt water; most fresh water is frozen in ice or underground.

  • The water cycle: evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration.
  • A watershed is all the land that drains into one body of water.
  • Large bodies of water like the Great Lakes moderate climate and cause lake-effect snow.
Example

What drives evaporation?

energy from the Sun

Answer: solar energy

Example

Where is most fresh water?

glaciers and ice caps

Answer: frozen in ice

Common mistakes

  • Thinking most of Earth's water is fresh.
  • Thinking groundwater is an underground lake.
  • Thinking a watershed is a building.

faq.a: All the land that drains into one river, lake or ocean. Ontario has many watersheds that flow to the Great Lakes, Hudson Bay or the St. Lawrence.

faq.q: Why are the Great Lakes important?
faq.a: They hold about one fifth of the world's surface fresh water and supply drinking water to millions of people.
Energy from the Sun evaporates water, and gravity pulls precipitation and runoff back down.

items.q: Liam notices this: Rainwater flows down a street into a storm drain. Which water cycle process is it?

items.q: Noah asks: what happens during infiltration?
c: Water flows over the land into streams, rivers and the ocean.
Water vapour cools and turns into tiny liquid droplets that form clouds.
Water soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.
Water falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
items.e: Infiltration: water soaks into the ground and becomes groundwater.

items.q: Which stage of the water cycle is this? The Sun warms water in seas, lakes and puddles, and it turns into water vapour.

c: Droplets join together and fall as rain, sleet, snow or hail.
The Sun warms water in seas, lakes and puddles, and it turns into water vapour.
Water runs into rivers, lakes, the sea and underground, and collects there.
Water vapour rises, cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.
items.e: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.

c: The Sun warms water in seas, lakes and puddles, and it turns into water vapour.

Water vapour rises, cools and turns into tiny droplets that form clouds.
Droplets join together and fall as rain, sleet, snow or hail.
items.e: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.

items.e: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.

items.q: Water has a very high heat capacity. Which effect on Earth's surface does this cause?
c: Oceans and lakes keep nearby climates milder.
Ice in cracks pries rocks apart (frost wedging).
Water rises through tiny spaces in soil by capillary action.
Rivers carve valleys and build deltas.
items.e: Water's unusual properties shape Earth's surface.

Liquid water flows downhill and carries particles.
